messages:
amal: FYI a customer asked for: WORM retention + legal hold support + ability to validate exported audit events cryptographically. They want to present validated exports to auditors. How do we stitch KMS + storage + schema together?
vikram: Short answer: S3 Object Lock (Compliance mode) + signed manifests. But there are nuances with customer-managed KMS keys + rotation.
jenna: We should define an explicit audit_schema version for this change. Adding fields for `signed_by`, `signature`, `sequence_id`, and `schema_version` seems necessary. keep it backward compatible.
sasha: Storage ops: recommended pattern = S3 (ObjectLock Compliance) for hot retention window, lifecycle to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term. ObjectLock survives lifecycle if Compliance mode set. Watch rehydration times for legal requests.
ops-oncall: For Private deployments customers will want CMKs (BYOK). We need a documented flow: create CMK, grant Redwood encryption/decrypt access for archival operations, then lock policies for rotation? note: if CMK is deleted/rotated improperly it can make data unreadable. request strong warnings. :warning: 
legal-team: Legal hold requirement: we need ability to tag objects with hold markers that override lifecycle expirations. Also exports used for eDiscovery must include chain-of-custody metadata.
vikram: Implementation thoughts: 1) Events are written to append-only store -> S3 objects with monotonically increasing `sequence_id`. 2) Periodic signed manifest files (signed using HSM-backed key) that include object ranges, hashes, and schema_version. 3) Store manifests in ObjectLock as well. The manifest proves immutability and integrity.
amal: For KMS rotation concerns — customers want key rotation but also proof audit events weren't altered. Rotating CMKs changes decrypt ability but not signatures if we sign with a separate signing key.
jenna: So separate concerns: encryption (KMS) vs integrity (signing). Add `integrity_signer` field referencing a signing key id (could be dedicated HSM or ECDSA key). Signatures stored in manifest, not per-event to reduce overhead.
sasha: Practical storage config: S3 bucket per-customer with ObjectLock enabled at creation. Lifecycle: 365d -> GLACIER 2 for cost. Retention handled by retention period + legal hold tag `x-redwood-legal-hold:true`. We should emit warnings when retention policies conflict.
ops-oncall: API hooks: admin endpoints to place/remove legal holds, but require audit trail + 2FA. Also expose `export/validate` endpoint that returns objects + manifest + signature so auditors can verify.
legal-team: Exports must include human-readable chain-of-custody summary and machine-checkable signature. Also provide guidance for subpoenas: time to rehydrate + who to contact.
vikram: Schema example snippet (proposal):
```json
{"schema_version":"audit_schema.v2","sequence_id":"0000000001","timestamp":"2026-03-10T14:02:01Z","actor":"amal@redwood.ai","action":"role.grant","resource":"project:prod","details":{"before":{},"after":{"role":"deploy"}},"event_hash":"sha256:..."}
```
Signed manifests contain array of `event_hash` + aggregate signature.
security-bot: Automated note: RFC 2026-03-10-audit-schema-v2 created by vikram, link: https://go/internal/rfcs/2026-03-audit-schema-v2 :page_facing_up:
amar: (typo: ama l)
jenna: One open question: PII in events. We must decide whether to sign raw events or a canonical, redacted representation. Signing raw events with PII risks customer concerns; signing redacted canonical forms + storing raw encrypted separately might be safer.
vikram: Agreed. Proposal: canonicalize -> redact PII fields -> compute `event_hash` -> store raw encrypted payload under KMS with tags referencing `event_id`. Raw payload not included in public export unless customer consents.
sasha: For BYOK customers we need to support CMK grants to our signing service if they want Redwood to sign. Alternatively customers can bring their own signing keys and we just store their signature materials. Need an API for customer-supplied manifests.
ops-oncall: Migration plan: start with schema opt-in flag `audit_export_signed:true` for a trial set of customers, run for 30d, iterate. Must add validation tests in CI that verify manifest->objects hash chain.
legal-team: Please add retention matrix to RFC: e.g., default 7y for audit events, emergency legal hold override, export SLA 5 business days for Glacier retrieval.
vikram: I'll draft RFC covering: schema v2, manifest design, object layout, signing key options (redwood-hsm, customer-supplied), retention/hold APIs, and migration plan. Will ping infra/security for design review.
amal: Thanks. Can we include a small PoC script for offline validation? e.g.:
```bash
# validate export
shasum -a 256 events/*.json > events.hashes
openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature manifest.sig events.hashes
```
jenna: love it. Put that in the RFC.
vikram: tagging this thread: needs-rfc-review, legal-review, infra-review :white_check_mark:
